_comment: ADOPT: the allowed-issuers registry — the attestation contract's key-distribution half (Loom 2.0 §6). core/attestations.mjs VERIFIES against this file: only attestations from an issuer listed here, checked by the named mechanism, count as authenticated. The ed25519 mechanism is verified in-process (real crypto, negative-tested); ci-oidc and sigstore mechanisms are verified by the platform in CI — until you wire them and record activation evidence, they report UNVERIFIED-HERE rather than silently passing. Own this file in CODEOWNERS by a non-builder group.

issuers.description: The protected CI runner's OIDC identity — gate evidence envelopes

SUPERSEDED for human approvals — human approval assertions now live in assertion-issuers.json (Factory Floor WS2 · D2.4), which is deliberately a SEPARATE registry so that a service key can never vouch for a person. Keep this entry only for service-issued envelopes; do not reuse its trust anchor in the assertion registry (the gate rejects a shared anchor).

verify.issuer: ADOPT: a SERVICE issuer — it must NOT be the identity provider used in assertion-issuers.json (the gate rejects a shared trust anchor)

issuers.description: DEMO reference issuer — a real ed25519 key pair; the private key is NOT shipped (regenerate your own; this one signs only the bundled example anchor). `demo: true` is refused by the ONE unified attestation stack (core/attestations.mjs, rc.36 D3) — every gate that verifies a signature refuses a demo issuer, the anchor gate included. The entry stays so the refusal is demonstrable; nothing can pass with it. Register your own signer (see evidence-example/regenerate.mjs for the per-run pattern). Issuer entries also honour `valid_from`/`valid_until`/`revoked`, and attestations may carry their own `validity` window.
